slides.title: Maus Crepe Insights
slides.hook: Turn robot camera checks into measurable crêpe-quality signals.
slides.tagline: Spread, fold, pose and run metrics from real robot records
slides.notes: Open with the value: turn robot run records and camera checks into a structured set of measurements. The public project includes the code and model artifacts; the Maus export stays private.

slides.title: What we can measure
caveats: Spread: diameter, area, centre offset and circularity.
Surface: robot-marked holes, uncovered plate, residue and browning.
Fold and pose: ideal-shape overlap, fold-area ratio, centre and axis angle.
Run context: stages, check attempts, outcomes and recipe settings.
slides.footer: Sources: private run tables + pipeline guide
slides.notes: The private export has 828 rows and 177 columns in runs.parquet. Vision.parquet has 138 rows. The current local export also has 257 push_off overlay attempts, with 248 passing the line detector's quality gate. Measurements include diameter, area, normalized centre offset, circularity, robot-marked holes, uncovered fraction, residue, CIE L* browning, ideal-fold IoU, folded area ratio, outline position and axis angle. Sources: the local aggregate export and documentation/data/pipeline.md. The push_off figures count attempts, not unique runs.

slides.title: Model metrics, with their scope
caveats: Teacher IoU compares with SAM 3 masks, not ground truth.
Human-mask review spans five runs on one robot; four were in student training.
Fold thresholds use the same passed-check frames; check-head labels are robot verdicts.
slides.notes: The segmentation student's 0.966 test IoU is against SAM 3 teacher masks on 225 frames from 57 held-out runs. The human comparison is median IoU 0.944 on 62 valid masks; it covers five consecutive runs of one robot, and four of those runs were in student training. The fold-state rule agrees with the robot's passed-check state on 991 frames, but thresholds were selected on those same frames, including the evaluation subset. Four check-verdict heads report balanced accuracy from 0.67 to 0.92 on holdouts of 31 to 61 frames; their labels are robot verdicts. Sources: code/models/crepe-student/model.json, documentation/vision/crepe-student.md and the check-verdict model cards. Repository: https://github.com/leonardoAB1/maus-crepe-insights.
